The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ is given above. Find ${f}^{′}(5).$

${f}^{′}(5)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To compute ${f}^{′}(5),$ we need to find the slope of the tangent to $f(x)$ at $x=5.$

Let's consider the graph of $y=f(x)$ for $x\in [4,6].$ Notice that $x=5$ lies in this interval.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252554/assets/42b4ddb29283047bd7ea8141ee14c793607b6b79a18f5d599a93839aec5a77b5.png)

The slope of $y=f(x)$ on $x\in (4,6)$ is constant and equals

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δf}{Δx} & =\frac{5-(-1)}{6-4}=\frac{6}{2}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(5)=3.$
